newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were $0.50 to $1.50 per cwt lower in light trading before the Independence Day holiday on Friday, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Several buying stations and packer buyers said they were out of the market following sales on Wednesday, with most packers said to have the hogs they need for Thursday's slaughter, sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $1.00 to $1.50 lower at $58.00-$58.50 in the country and $59.00-$59.50 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said.

A buyer for a large packer in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area said his company already was booking hogs steady to $0.50 below Thursday's prices at $58.00 in the country and $58.50-$59.00 at plants for Monday delivery.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $58.00-$59.00 in the country and $59.00-$59.50 at plants in thin volume.
"We're basically out of it for today and packers aren't chasing after the hogs very hard," a central Illinois buyer said.
Indiana/Ohio hogs sold $1.00 lower at $57.00-$58.00 in the country and $59.00-$59.50 at plants.
Major hog slaughter plants will be closed Friday in observance of the holiday and a small number will be open on Saturday, company and market sources said.
